column3: Close to the Hebrew; “his day” is expanded to “the day of his birth.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a man has been conceived” is rendered “A male child is conceived.”
Close to the Hebrew; “may God not care for it” is rendered “May God above not seek it.”
Close to the Hebrew; וְצַלְמָוֶת (“deep darkness”) is rendered “the shadow of death.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the eyelids of dawn” is rendered “the dawning of the day.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the doors of my womb” is clarified as “my mother’s womb.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV renders the past-tense verbs as hypothetical, “I would have lain still.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “why” to continue the question of v11.
Close to the Hebrew; “joyful to exultation” is rendered “rejoice exceedingly.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV repeats “Why is light given” from v20, and וַיָּסֶךְ (“hedged in”) is rendered “hedged in.”
Close to the Hebrew; “before my food” is rendered “before I eat.”
